prize_parts.citation: For developing targeted protein degradation by induced proximity, through heterobifunctional PROTAC degraders and the identification of cereblon as the target of thalidomide-type molecular glue degraders, which direct the ubiquitin-proteasome system to chosen proteins

statement.case_for: After round 1 I keep B019 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa. It is the only configuration that more than one member supports, and the support is for the discovery, not just for a name: five of us name the same principle, a small molecule that forms a ternary complex between an E3 ligase and a chosen protein so that degradation becomes a designable chemical event. The structural evidence is what persuades me most. Ternary-complex crystal structures show how the induced interface and its cooperativity are built, and cereblon structures bound to thalidomide-type compounds show how a glue reshapes a surface to recruit neosubstrates. Both strands therefore converge on one mechanism, E3 ligase recruitment, which is why I think a single citation is defensible and honest. Crews and Deshaies supply the concept and first demonstrations. Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, which turned an empirical drug story into a molecular mechanism and is the reason the glue strand can sit under the same citation. The citation names the principle and two mechanistic pillars, and does not depend on any one drug approval.
statement.case_against: Clinical delivery is still incomplete, as far as I know no degrader is approved, and I cannot settle that from the supplied files. Credit is crowded: Ciulli, Sakamoto, Gray, Ito and Kim all have real claims, and a three-name cap forces a line that some will see as arbitrary, in particular between the PROTAC and glue strands. The first PROTAC used a peptide ligand with poor cell permeability, so the early work was proof of concept and the drug-like version came later, which weakens a claim of sole conceptual origin for Crews and Deshaies. Ordered mesoporous silica (B005), my opening first choice, remains the more mature and structurally cleaner story, but no colleague supports it and Linke's generative-reach and credit-lineage questions are not yet answered, so I do not push it as a final position.

responses.point: Aqvist keeps B019 but takes Ciulli as third laureate with a PROTAC-only citation about heterobifunctional small molecules, and treats the cereblon and glue strand as a separate discovery.
responses.response: I considered this seriously, since Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures are exactly the structure-guided design work I value. I still prefer Handa. The chair's question is whether the third name adds a discovery the citation depends on. Handa's cereblon identification is a target discovery that explains thalidomide and opened the glue class, whereas VHL ligand design, important as it is, is a major advance within the PROTAC framework Crews and Deshaies already set. A PROTAC-only trio would invite the objection that the people who explained thalidomide are missing, and you concede that in your case against. If the committee voted to restrict the citation to PROTACs, I could accept Ciulli, but I would regard that as narrowing the achievement.

responses.point: Somfai doubts that PROTACs and glues belong in one citation and asks what is chemically new, while preferring Ciulli over a mixed trio if one must choose.
responses.response: On one versus two achievements, my answer is that the two strands are one mechanism reached from two directions: both recruit an E3 ligase to a protein that it would not normally degrade. A two-part prize does not fit under the three-person cap without dropping a name from either part, so it would be worse, not cleaner. On what is chemically new, it is a design principle in which induced proximity and neo-interface formation are engineered with ligand chemistry, not a new reaction. I also remain unconvinced that B034 beats this case, since the 2010 cross-coupling prize covers the transformation class and Kosugi's earlier work clouds priority.

responses.point: Sparr prefers ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B045), but asks whether B019 should win if clinical approval is not required, and flags the risk of a second pandemic-vaccine prize.
responses.response: I think the answer to your question is yes. Approved products are a legitimate argument for maturity, and I respect that B045 has them, but approval is not our criterion. The chair's question for you is the credit problem, and I do not see how the trio resolves it: Madden, MacLachlan and Langer have claims comparable to Hope and Anderson, and you state yourself that much of the optimisation was empirical screening. I would also read B045 as nearer to delivery engineering than to a new chemical principle. I appreciate that you disclosed your field bias, and I would ask whether your reservations about B019 are reasons to wait or only a different weighting of approval.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks B055 first and B019 seventh because no PROTAC is approved and the two strands may need separate recognition, listing B019 as an alternative.
responses.response: This is the clearest test of the maturity question. You ask for delivered evidence, but mechanism and independent confirmation across many laboratories are strong here, and long-range electron transfer was itself recognised for its principle before any application. My view is that the Marcus 1992 prize covers the theoretical core of B055, so Gray and Winkler would need a distinct-discovery argument, and Dutton, Moser and Onuchic priority is unresolved. For B019 I would accept as evidence of delivery what we already have: structures of ternary complexes and cereblon-drug complexes, and many independent reproductions. If you would support B019 given a citation that rests on mechanism, I think the current wording meets that.

responses.point: Linke asks whether mesoporous silica (B005) opened a capability comparable to degraders or nanopores, and notes that its credit lineage (Mobil, FSM-16, SBA) needs an answer; he also keeps a maturity reservation on B019.
responses.response: Fair challenge. Mesoporous silica opened a materials class with tunable pores in the 2 to 50 nm range, which made it possible to host large molecules, which then led to ordered mesoporous carbons, metal oxides and a new template-design logic. Its legacy is more than a support, but it is a materials platform, not a new capability like removing a protein. I also cannot give a clean three-name answer between Kresge and Beck, Inagaki, Ryoo and Zhao. So I do not push B005 ahead of B019. On your maturity reservation, none of us has seen approval, but the nanopore case shows that maturity does not remove the attribution problem, and the B019 attribution problem is smaller.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept Handa, Crews and Deshaies as a defensible cut of a crowded field, or whether Ciulli, Sakamoto, Gray or Ito will seem the more obvious omission.
Whether durable clinical efficacy of a degrader should matter before recognition; I have assumed not, but cannot verify the approval status.
Whether a single citation can cover PROTACs and glues without being read as two prizes merged.
I am relying on memory of the history of several fields, including priority details of the first PROTAC and of cereblon, and have not verified them.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with B019 or any credited name. Scientific closeness to B005 and B006 (porous materials, electron crystallography) as disclosed in round 1; neither is in my final configuration, and B005 appears only as an alternative. I have no personal or institutional link to any named candidate. Stockholm University colleagues, including Secretary Brzezinski, are not candidates.
